description: Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a beloved classic from the Liguria region of Italy, known for its irresistibly soft, airy texture and savory crisp crust. This traditional flatbread is generously drizzled with premium olive oil, sprinkled with fragrant rosemary, and finished with coarse sea salt, making it perfect as an appetizer, side, or light meal. Its simplicity highlights the quality of its few ingredients, delivering an unforgettable taste of Genoa.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water (300ml) with the granulated sugar and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the all-purpose flour and fine sea salt to the foamy yeast mixture. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface.

instructions.title: Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Knead the dough for about 8-10 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. If using a stand mixer, use the dough hook attachment and knead on medium speed for 6-8 minutes.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Lightly grease a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare for Baking
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Drizzle 2 tablespoons of olive oil onto a 9x13 inch baking sheet and spread it evenly. Gently punch down the risen dough and transfer it to the prepared baking sheet. Gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to tear it.

instructions.title: Dimple and Top
instructions.text: Using your fingertips, create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough. In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil and 2 tablespoons of warm water to create an emulsion. Pour this mixture evenly over the dimpled dough. Sprinkle with chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Bake
instructions.text: Let the focaccia rise again on the baking sheet for another 20-30 minutes. Then, bake in the preheated oven for 25-35 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through.

instructions.title: Serve Warm
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven. If desired, drizzle with a little more fresh extra virgin olive oil immediately after baking for extra flavor and shine. Let it cool slightly on a wire rack before slicing and serving warm. Enjoy!

tips: For an extra airy focaccia, ensure your dough is quite wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add too much extra flour during kneading. A higher hydration leads to a more open crumb.
Always use a high-quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the final drizzle. It makes a significant difference in the flavor profile of your Focaccia Genovese.
Focaccia is best enjoyed warm, fresh from the oven. If you have leftovers, a quick reheat in a toaster oven or conventional oven will bring back its delicious crispness.
article:
Focaccia is more than just bread; it's an experience, a canvas for the simple yet profound flavors of Italian cuisine. Among its many regional variations, one stands out for its elegant simplicity and sheer deliciousness: Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil. This flatbread, hailing from the Ligurian coast, is a testament to how a few high-quality ingredients can create something truly extraordinary. With its dimpled surface, fragrant rosemary, generous slick of olive oil, and satisfyingly chewy yet crisp texture, it’s a staple of Italian baking that has captured hearts worldwide.

Originating from Genoa, the capital of Liguria, this focaccia is steeped in history and local tradition. It's not just a dish; it's a part of the daily rhythm, enjoyed for breakfast, as a snack, or alongside meals. Forget the thick, bready versions you might find elsewhere; authentic Focaccia Genovese is relatively thin, with a delicate balance between a slightly crispy bottom and a soft, airy interior. Making it at home is a wonderfully rewarding process, bringing the aromatic charm of an Italian bakery right into your kitchen.

## What is Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil?

At its heart, Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a yeast-leavened flatbread characterized by its distinct texture and flavor profile. Unlike many other breads, it boasts a remarkably high hydration level, resulting in a very wet, sticky dough that ultimately yields an incredibly tender crumb. The signature dimples pressed into the dough before baking are not just for aesthetics; they create pockets that trap the luscious olive oil and coarse sea salt, ensuring every bite is bursting with flavor.

The "Genovese" part of its name specifically refers to its origin in Genoa, distinguishing it from other regional focaccia styles. What makes it particularly special is the emphasis on high-quality ingredients: robust extra virgin olive oil, fresh rosemary, and a good flaky sea salt are non-negotiable. The crust is often golden brown and slightly crisp, while the interior remains soft and airy, almost cloud-like. It’s a versatile bread, simple enough to be enjoyed plain, yet robust enough to accompany a wide range of dishes. The authentic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil truly embodies the spirit of Ligurian cuisine – simple, fresh, and utterly delicious.

## Ingredients You Need

Mastering Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil starts with selecting the right ingredients. Quality truly matters here, as the simplicity of the recipe allows each component to shine.

*   **Strong Bread Flour (Type 00 or All-Purpose with high protein):** About 500g. A higher protein content helps develop gluten, giving the focaccia its characteristic chewiness and structure.
*   **Warm Water:** Around 400ml (about 105-115°F or 40-46°C). The warmth activates the yeast.
*   **Active Dry Yeast:** 7g (one packet or about 2 ¼ teaspoons). This is the leavening agent that makes the focaccia rise.
*   **Sugar:** A pinch (about ½ teaspoon). Feeds the yeast, helping it activate.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** 10g (about 1 ½ teaspoons) for the dough. Enhances flavor.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** Approximately 100-150ml, divided. This is perhaps the most crucial ingredient. Use a good quality, fruity olive oil for maximum flavor in the dough, for greasing the pan, and for drizzling generously over the top.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs, needles stripped and roughly chopped. Provides that quintessential aromatic flavor.
*   **Flaky Sea Salt (like Maldon):** For sprinkling on top before baking. Adds a delightful crunch and burst of salinity.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a rewarding process that requires patience but is surprisingly straightforward.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water and a pinch of sugar. Sprinkle the active dry yeast over the top. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Pour in about 30ml of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy, very sticky dough forms. Do not add more flour, even if it seems too wet; this high hydration is key.
3.  **Knead (or No-Knead Option):** You can knead this dough by hand for 10-15 minutes on a lightly oiled surface until it becomes more elastic, or use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 5-7 minutes. Alternatively, for a no-knead approach, simply mix thoroughly, then perform a series of "stretch and folds" every 30 minutes for 2 hours (wet your hands, grab a portion of the dough, stretch it up, and fold it over itself).
4.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Transfer the dough to a clean, well-oiled bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally grease a 9x13 inch (or similar size) baking pan with at least 50ml of extra virgin olive oil. Ensure the sides are well coated.
6.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently transfer the risen dough into the prepared pan. Using oiled hands, carefully stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. If it resists, let it rest for 10-15 minutes before continuing to stretch.
7.  **Second Rise:** Once the dough fills the pan, cover it again and let it rise for another 30-45 minutes in a warm place. It should look puffy and airy.
8.  **Dimple the Dough:** Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). With well-oiled fingers, gently press deep dimples all over the surface of the dough, taking care not to push all the way through to the bottom of the pan. These dimples are crucial for trapping the oil and creating a beautiful texture.
9.  **Final Toppings:** Drizzle the remaining 50-70ml of extra virgin olive oil generously over the dimpled surface. Scatter the chopped fresh rosemary and flaky sea salt evenly over the top.
10. **Bake:** Bake for 20-30 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom crust is crisp.
11. **Cool:** Carefully remove the Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil from the pan immediately and transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. Serve warm or at room temperature.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil isn't just about following the steps; a few expert tips can elevate your baking to professional levels.

*   **Don't Skimp on Olive Oil:** This is perhaps the most crucial tip. Focaccia Genovese is renowned for its generous use of extra virgin olive oil. It contributes to the flavor, the crispy crust, and the tender crumb. Use a good quality oil, and don't be afraid to use a lot – in the dough, to grease the pan, and as a lavish drizzle before baking.
*   **High Hydration is Key:** The dough will be very wet and sticky, almost like a thick batter. Resist the urge to add more flour! This high hydration is what gives the focaccia its characteristic airy, open crumb. Oiled hands are your best friend when handling it.
*   **Patience with Proofing:** Allow ample time for both rises. Proper fermentation develops flavor and texture. A warm (but not hot) environment is ideal for rising. If your kitchen is cool, place the dough in a slightly warm oven (turned off, with just the light on) or near a sunny window.
*   **Deep Dimples:** When dimpling the dough, use all your fingers and press down firmly, almost to the bottom of the pan. These deep indentations are essential for creating those delightful pockets that hold the olive oil and salt, resulting in bursts of flavor in every bite.
*   **Hot Oven:** A high oven temperature ensures a quick rise and a beautifully crisp crust while keeping the interior moist. Preheat your oven thoroughly before baking.
*   **Fresh Rosemary & Flaky Salt:** Fresh rosemary provides an incomparable aroma and flavor. Dried rosemary can be used in a pinch, but fresh is far superior. Flaky sea salt not only looks beautiful but also adds a wonderful textural contrast and bursts of salinity.

## Serving Suggestions

The beauty of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil lies in its versatility. It can be the star of the show or a delightful accompaniment.

*   **Appetizer:** Serve warm with a simple dish of high-quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping, perhaps with a splash of balsamic vinegar. It's also fantastic with a selection of olives, cured meats, and cheeses.
*   **With Meals:** It makes an excellent sidekick to hearty soups, stews, or fresh salads. Its robust flavor stands up well to rich dishes, while its lightness complements lighter fare.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill it with your favorite sandwich ingredients – think prosciutto and mozzarella, grilled vegetables, or a simple tomato and basil.
*   **Breakfast/Brunch:** A warm slice of Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil with a cup of coffee is a surprisingly delightful start to the day. Some even enjoy it with a smear of ricotta or a soft-boiled egg.
*   **Just as a Snack:** Honestly, it's so good straight out of the oven, simply torn into pieces and savored on its own. The aroma alone is intoxicating!

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfect as is, there's always room for creative twists once you've mastered the basic recipe.

*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, feel free to experiment with other fresh herbs like thyme, oregano, or a mix of "herbes de Provence."
*   **Vegetable Toppings:** Before the final rise and dimpling, you can press thinly sliced cherry tomatoes, red onions, black olives, or even thinly sliced potatoes directly into the dough.
*   **Garlic Infusion:** Mince a few cloves of garlic and mix them with the olive oil before drizzling it over the focaccia for an extra aromatic kick.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan or Pecorino Romano can be added with the flaky salt for a savory, cheesy crust.
*   **Sweet Focaccia:** For a less traditional but delightful treat, omit the rosemary and flaky salt. Instead, sprinkle with sugar and perhaps some thinly sliced fruit (like grapes or figs) or toasted nuts before baking.
*   **Gluten-Free Option:** While achieving the exact texture can be challenging, a blend of gluten-free flours (like rice flour, tapioca starch, and sorghum flour) combined with a binder like xanthan gum can be used. Adjust water content as needed, as gluten-free flours absorb liquids differently.

Making Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is a journey into the heart of Italian baking – simple ingredients, mindful preparation, and incredible flavor. Whether you stick to the classic or venture into creative variations, this fragrant, dimpled flatbread is sure to become a beloved staple in your kitchen, bringing a taste of Liguria right to your table. Enjoy the process, and savor every delicious bite!
